keyVerseText: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
rootMeaning: The word πότερον (póteron) is the neuter form of a comparative derived from the base of ποῦ (poû), which means 'where' or 'whither.' This etymology suggests that πότερον originally carried the sense of choosing between two alternatives related to place or direction, but it evolved into an adverb used to inquire 'which of two' possibilities is the case. Thus, beyond the simple English 'whether,' πότερον conveys a precise comparison or choice between two distinct options, emphasizing the act of discerning between alternatives.
usageInScripture: πότερον occurs only once in the New Testament, specifically in John 7:17, where it is translated as 'whether.' Its singular usage highlights its function as an interrogative adverb introducing a choice between two possibilities. This consistency in translation underscores πότερον's role in framing direct or indirect questions that ask for clarification between two alternatives, reinforcing the importance of decision or discernment in the scriptural context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πότερον as a word that marks a choice between two alternatives enriches our grasp of biblical inquiry and revelation. It reminds believers that faith often involves discerning between competing claims or teachings, calling for a deliberate decision grounded in truth. This word highlights the personal responsibility to seek God's will and to recognize divine truth as distinct from human opinion. Thus, πότερον encourages believers to engage actively with Scripture and the Spirit's guidance, fostering a faith that is both thoughtful and obedient.
keyVerseReflection: In John 7:17, Jesus says, 'If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.' Here, πότερον introduces the critical choice between two sources of teaching—divine or self-originated. This word sharpens the contrast and invites the listener to discern the true origin of Jesus' teaching. It underscores the promise that obedience to God's will leads to spiritual insight, enabling believers to distinguish God's word from human ideas.
